description:
## Outcome

The Mix application version is the only Jido release version source. CLI output, cache paths, run manifests, artifact names, tags, and release metadata read that value. The fast `--version` path reads it without starting `:jido_cli` or provider applications.

## Why now

A second product version can make a tag, command, package, and manifest disagree. A version lookup that starts the application can also remove the measured fast-dispatch gain.

## Work

1. Add a small release identity boundary that reads the compiled application version.
2. Remove the CLI version constant and update `jido --version`, escript cache naming, and automation manifests.
3. Keep the exact `--version` command on the fast dispatcher. Do not run credential checks or `Application.ensure_all_started/1`.
4. Make documentation and package scripts use the same source.
5. Add a tag validator for exact `v<application-version>` agreement.
6. Report the Jido version, Jidoka version, Elixir version, and OTP version through one tested runtime API.
7. Add an architecture test that rejects a second product SemVer literal in production source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mix.exs` owns the only Jido product version value.
- [ ] `jido --version` and JSONL manifest version fields match the application version.
- [ ] A mismatched release tag fails before build or publication.
- [ ] Source, escript, and release builds report the same value.
- [ ] Exact `--version` does not start `:jido_cli`, credential checks, or provider applications.
- [ ] Tests can inject version data without changing global application state.

## Tests

Extend CLI and automation plan tests. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not create a second version file. Do not infer the version from Git at runtime. Protocol schema versions remain separate integers.
title: Make the Mix application version the only release version source
